career_spells.role: Economics lecturer; unit leader and course coordinator (archived handbook observations)
career_spells.evidence_note: Own biography confirms lecturing; Yale records Monash placement in 2004–05 cohort. Contract start/end, hours and historical institutional control require follow-up; do not convert placement cohort into exact employment dates. A Monash-hosted paper dated31August2005 supplies a contemporaneous Department of Economics affiliation, but no appointment start/end or hours. An Australian Financial Review article published 17 June 2006 identifies him contemporaneously as a Monash economics lecturer, extending the dated observation beyond the August 2005 paper; it still does not establish appointment boundaries, contract type or hours. Archived university handbooks name him as leader of ECC4369 offered in second semester 2006 and economics coordinator of the Graduate Diploma in Economic Studies in the 2008 handbook. These are dated handbook observations, not proof of continuous employment between 2005 and 2008 or exact commencement/cessation. The 2008 page has a later maintenance timestamp; this does not establish continued employment in 2017. Unit contact hours and student full-time course duration are not his paid weekly hours or FTE. Possible overlap with Nous from June2008 requires appointment/leave evidence.

2026-09-29 initial pass inspected APH indexed biography, first speech, own biography, Yale placement archive, April/July 2013 Pottinger publications, ACFS 2013 author profile and 2015 annual review, 2018 conference host biography and 2026 publisher biography. LinkedIn https://au.linkedin.com/in/danielmulinomp returned 429; deferred, no bypass or paid alternative.

Targeted searches for Monash 2006, Nous chronology, CV, full-time economist work and Federal Reserve research produced no admissible full-time evidence. A 2006 workshop chair listing and research publication affiliations are leads, not contract-duration proof. Excluded contact-aggregation profiles and unrelated full-time job advertisements.

A 2026 author biography explicitly calls overseas engagements internships, while earlier professional biography uses consultant/research descriptions. Preserve the ambiguity and do not assume they were unpaid, salaried, continuous or full-time. Yale teaching appears in secondary biography and needs primary appointment verification.

Year-level early departmental dates remain intact. No durations calculated from titles or sequential labels. Missing intervals, including 1996–1997 and state-to-federal transition, remain unknown rather than unemployment. Party membership/policy committee activity and campaigning are separate from paid employment; blocked initial record is not completion.

Direct LinkedIn was not retried after429. Targeted searches for employer dates and Monash roles yielded no full-time evidence; generic exact-site searches were inconsistent, so retrieval method is explicit. McKinsey2019 automation report advisory committee and Curtin Research Centre advisory council are governance leads, not evidence of salaried consulting or a2018–19 employment bridge. 2026-10-03 follow-up: official Victorian Parliament history narrows state elected service to 28 November 2014–22 November 2018 and lists both parliamentary secretary appointments from 30 November 2014 to 17 December 2018. The appointment endpoint after the elected-term endpoint is recorded as a source detail, not converted into a separate employment spell. AEC final results support federal service from the 18 May 2019 election. The remaining inter-parliamentary interval is therefore 23 November 2018–17 May 2019 for research purposes; targeted 2018–19 employment/consulting searches found only candidacy, campaigning and governance/advisory material, not paid work. Do not label the interval unemployment. Monash, Nous/Pottinger hours, early departments and US internship status remain unresolved.

Together with the 31 August 2005 Monash paper, this materially brackets observed affiliation across those dates, but neither source supplies appointment commencement/cessation, contract type, hours or leave. Targeted 2018–19 bridge, ministerial-adviser and consulting searches found no paid employment for the inter-parliamentary gap; candidacy and governance material remain excluded.
